data.name: Call of Juarez: Bound in Blood
data.detailed_description:
O VELHO OESTE, 1864. Para salvar a sua família, os irmãos McCall estão dispostos a matar todos os que se atravessem entre eles e o lendário Ouro de Juarez. Mas quando o fascínio do dinheiro e das mulheres testa a sua ligação, será que os laços familiares vão resistir?



  • Torna-te num pistoleiro — coleciona todo um arsenal de armas, desde revólveres até canhões de grande calibre e metralhadoras. Cada tiro preciso aumenta o teu foco, o que te permite entrar em modos de tiro letais quando estiveres em desvantagem e que pode chegar ao apogeu quando os irmãos disparam juntos.

  • Irmãos com armas — joga com Ray ou Thomas, cada um com o seu próprio estilo de jogo (corpo a corpo ou combate à distância), habilidades (laço, dinamite etc) e um arsenal mortífero (armas duplas, carabinas de longa distância etc). Tira vantagem dos seus pontos fortes e tenta sobreviver aos combates mais brutais alguma vez imaginados.

  • Experiência imersiva do faroeste — explora as paisagens naturais do Oeste Selvagem a pé, a cavalo e em carruagens e canoas. Visita locais icónicos repletos de bandidos. Os irmãos McCall enfrentam um chefe apache renegado, um fora da lei mexicano ganancioso e um coronel vingativo. E estes são apenas alguns dos vilões que vais encontrar pelo teu caminho.

Atenção: as opções online deste jogo foram descontinuadas em agosto de 2016. Os modos cooperativo e multijogador online não estarão disponíveis.

  • Sound: DirectX 9-compatible sound card
  • Peripherals Supported: Windows-compliant keyboard, mouse, gamepads

  • ATI RADEON X1650-1950 / HD 2400-2900 / 3650-3870 / 4650-4870 series
  • NVIDIA GeForce 6800 / 7600-7950 / 8600-8800 / GTX 260-280 series

reviews.review:
This is the first sequel to the immersive western game '[b]Call Of Juarez[/b]'.  If you played that game, then you will be quite comfortable here, as this game is exactly more-of-the-same of what the first game had ([i]choice of 2 playable main characters, combat mechanics, keyboard controls, graphics, etc[/i]).  For reference, I've included my '[b]Call Of Juarez[/b]' review at the bottom.

Although this game itself is a sequel, the story is a prequel.  It starts about 18 to 20 years before the events in the first game.  In the first game, you played as either Ray McCall ([i]known then as Reverend Ray[/i]), or Billy Candle ([i]Thomas McCall's step-son[/i]).  In this game, you play as either Ray McCall, or his brother Thomas McCall.  They are Confederate soldiers in the Civil War around 1864.

Then they hear that a well-known Union commander, General Sherman, is marching through Georgia to the sea and burning down everything in his path.  They quickly realize that their family homestead is in General Sherman's path.  Thus, they desert the Confederate army to go save their mother, their younger brother William, and their home.  Their commanding officer, Colonel Barnsby, swears that after the war is over he will personally hunt them down and see them hang high for being deserters.

The brothers arrive one day late, finding their home with lots of damage and their mother dead.  They get William and head west, vowing to return one day to reclaim their land and rebuild their home.  They are both angry men now, liking liquor, women, and trouble a little too much.  Ray & Thomas seem to leave a trail of bodies everywhere that they go, so eventually the Pinkertons are on their trail.

([i]FYI, in real life, the Pinkerton Company was founded in the early 1850's, and was the largest private law enforcement company in the world from the 1870's to the 1890's.[/i])  Their brother William is a reverend who constantly lectures them about their evil ways, and pleads with them to change.  To escape the Pinkertons, Ray & Thomas cross the border into Mexico, as many wild west outlaws did.

Once there, they hear that the legendary gold of Juarez is actually real, and decide that getting ahold of that gold would provide them the financial means to finally go back to Georgia, rebuild their home, and settle down.  Of course, things don't go as planned.  They end up tangling with regular townfolk, local law enforcement, random outlaws, Mexican bandits, and 3 different Native American tribes.

In addition, throw into the mix a powerful force which is capable of tearing 2 brothers apart...  a sexy woman that both of them are lusting over.  The plot of the first game was good, but this one is better.  Personally, I think this one would have made a great movie.  Like the first one, this game also has 15 episodes, and also has slightly different skill sets between the 2 playable characters of Ray & Thomas.

You must play as Ray for Chapter #1, and must play as Thomas for Chapter #2.  Then you can choose which character to play from Chapters #3 to #13.  In Chapter #14 you will play as both, and for Chapter #15 you again can choose who to play.  The quick-draw duels are still a problem to get through, and several forum posts complain the game does not launch with newer computers and video cards.

Personally, the game randomly crashed on me once, but that was the only glitch of any kind that I experienced.  The graphics still look mostly okay in 2026, but are a little on the janky side in some places.  There are no trading cards, no achievements, and no Point Shop items.  The game menu still has an option for multi-player, but apparently the official servers have not had support for 10 years or so.

There are also menu options to download extra maps and extra missions, but I don't know if those work or not.  I did not bother to try them.  There are 4 difficulty levels available, but you must beat the game once to unlock the hardest difficulty.  I again enjoyed both the story and the gameplay, but was again disappointed in the length of the game.  It was a little shorter than the first game was.

For most people, the game should only take 8 to 10 hours to complete, depending on your shooting skills and pace of exploration.  It could take several hours longer if you want to torture yourself by going out of your way to try to find the 89 "[i]secrets[/i]".  There is no reward for finding them though, so I did not bother to go out of my way.  I just found the ones which were on, or close to, the main path.


My '[b]Call Of Juarez[/b]' review...
